temperature.title: Right amount, right interval
temperature.description: Grease = base oil held in a thickener; the bearing takes oil from it. Too little starves the bearing; too much churns and overheats it (temperature rises for hours after over-greasing). Relubricate with a quantity G ≈ 0.005 × D × B (grams; D = OD, B = width in mm) at intervals from the maker's charts (speed factor n·dm, temperature, contamination), with the relief plug open so old grease can escape. Never mix incompatible thickeners.

video_tutorials.title: Grease Lubrication System — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Grease Lubrication System.
Grease lubrication feeds a rolling bearing with grease — base oil held in a thickener — through a grease nipple, by hand with a grease gun or automatically with a single-point lubricator.
A relief plug lets old grease escape so the housing does not over-pressurise or overfill.
Typical applications include plummer blocks on conveyors, fans and crushers; electric motor bearings and outdoor machinery.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Split Plummer-Block Housing (cap & base), Shaft (turning).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Grease Lubrication System works.
Fresh grease enters through the nipple.
It reaches the rolling elements.
Old grease purges through the relief.
An automatic lubricator doses continuously.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Grease = base oil held in a thickener; the bearing takes oil from it.

video_tutorials.title: Grease Lubrication System — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Grease Lubrication System.
Check lubricator level / bearing temperature.
Relubricate per schedule.
Clean housing; replace grease & seals.
Watch for over-greasing: high temperature after greasing. Common cause: too much grease, relief closed.
Watch for starvation: noise, heat. Common cause: missed greasing, empty lubricator.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
